name: Non-distal Deletion 12q Syndrome

criteria.description: Identification of interstitial deletion involving the proximal or middle segment of the long arm of chromosome 12 (12q) by chromosomal microarray or karyotyping
Presence of characteristic craniofacial dysmorphisms including hypertelorism, broad nasal bridge, and micrognathia
Global developmental delay or intellectual disability of variable severity
Presence of congenital malformations such as cardiac defects or skeletal abnormalities
Postnatal growth retardation or failure to thrive

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Genetic confirmation of 12q interstitial deletion plus presence of at least two major clinical features including distinctive facial features and developmental delay
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on genetic testing due to phenotypic variability.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism including hypertelorism and broad nasal bridge
searchTerms: wide-set eyes and broad nose bridge
facial features with hypertelorism and broad nasal bridge
distinct facial shape with spaced eyes and wide nose

pathognomonic.symptomName: Global developmental delay with intellectual disability
searchTerms: global developmental delay with intellectual disability
slow growth in skills and cognition

pathognomonic.symptomName: Interstitial deletion involving proximal or middle 12q region confirmed by genetic testing
pathognomonic.notes: Genetic hallmark rather than clinical symptom
searchTerms: missing DNA segment in 12q proximal or middle area
confirmed 12q interstitial deletion by genetic test

common.symptomName: Congenital heart defects including ventricular septal defects
Skeletal anomalies including clinodactyly or brachydactyly
searchTerms: finger bone abnormalities like curved or short fingers
skeletal anomalies with clinodactyly or brachydactyly
breathing problems with repeated lung infections

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible metabolic screening abnormalities in some cases
imaging: Skeletal X-rays showing clinodactyly or other anomalies
Brain MRI may show nonspecific findings related to developmental delay
genetic: Interstitial deletion of chromosome 12q confirmed by chromosomal microarray or FISH
Breakpoint mapping to proximal or middle long arm of chromosome 12
other: Developmental and neuropsychological assessments confirming intellectual disability

distinguishingFeatures: Deletion involves distal 12q region rather than proximal/middle
Different facial dysmorphisms and clinical presentation
Deletion on chromosome 6q with overlapping but distinct phenotypic features
Different genetic locus confirmed by testing

redFlags: Severe congenital heart defects requiring early intervention
references: Smith et al., 2018. Clinical and molecular characterization of interstitial 12q deletions. Am J Med Genet A.
